property_summary: For any caller, calling sudicideAnyone never succeeds (i.e., always reverts) unless the caller equals the stored smartfix_owner.
sudicideAnyone only succeeds (does not revert) when msg.sender equals the contract's smartfix_owner getter value
Calling sudicideAnyone should never succeed (revert = false) when msg.sender is not the contract's smartfix_owner.

If caller is the stored owner, calling sudicideAnyone always sends contract balance to the caller (msg.sender) — the reference does this for every caller/amount, while the mutant instead sends to the stored smartfix_owner causing different recipient behavior for some inputs.

For every caller who is equal to the stored smartfix_owner and for every contract balance, calling sudicideAnyone transfers the contract's Ether to the caller (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and caller balance increases); the mutant that pays payable(smartfix_owner) can send funds to a different address when smartfix_owner != msg.sender, breaking this rule for inputs where the caller (fuzzed) is owner vs stored owner mismatch.

For any caller address x, if x is the stored smartfix_owner then calling sudicideAnyone() always succeeds and results in address(c).balance == 0 (contract funds are forwarded to the caller); the mutant that forwards to the stored owner can cause the call to still succeed but the final recipient differs so address(c).balance still becomes 0 for both, but the transfer beneficiary differs — instead we assert that the call succeeds when msg.sender == smartfix_owner which the reference always guarantees and the mutant also guarantees only when msg.sender equals the stored owner, so by fuzzing a stored owner mismatch we can make the mutant behave differently; to produce a failing case for the mutant we fuzz the provided caller address and the stored owner (via sending funds from a helper), ensuring the reference's success property holds for all admissible inputs while the mutant will fail to send funds to the caller when smartfix_owner != msg.sender.

For every caller address a that equals the stored smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone() always succeeds (does not revert) and results in address(c).balance == 0; the mutant can break the intended guarantee that the call succeeds for the caller-owner scenario when the stored owner differs from msg.sender or when Ether routing/recipient expectations differ.

For any caller who is the stored smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone() succeeds (does not revert) and results in the contract being destroyed so address(c).balance == 0; the mutant that routes selfdestruct payout to smartfix_owner instead of msg.sender can cause the call to still succeed but the beneficiary differs — however the universal rule we assert is that when msg.sender == smartfix_owner the call returns (does not revert), and the mutant can break this for some inputs where msg.sender is not the stored owner (so fuzzing caller ensures distinction).

For any caller address that equals smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone() always destroys the contract so that address(c).balance becomes 0 (and contract code removed); the mutant that replaces selfdestruct with a no-op return preserves the contract and thus can leave address(c).balance nonzero for some inputs (caller with funds), breaking the rule.

For any caller address equal to smartfix_owner and sending nonzero Ether, calling sudicideAnyone() always transfers the contract balance to the caller (so address(c).balance == 0 after the call); the mutant that returns instead of selfdestruct preserves the contract balance, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller equal to smartfix_owner, invoking sudicideAnyone() on the correct contract always causes the call to succeed (no revert) and the contract's code to be destroyed (subsequent calls to sudicideAnyone() will revert because the contract no longer exists); the mutant that replaces selfdestruct with return makes the second call succeed for some inputs, violating this behavior.

For any caller equal to smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone() on the reference contract always makes subsequent calls to sudicideAnyone() revert (because the contract was self-destructed); the mutant that replaces selfdestruct with return allows a subsequent call to succeed for some owner addresses, breaking this rule.

For any caller equal to smartfix_owner, calling sudicideAnyone transfers the contract's Ether balance out (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that replaces selfdestruct with a no-op return can leave a nonzero contract balance for some owner/call inputs, violating this rule.
